reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) confirms in-situ TiC formation and dispersion strengthening in WTaTiVCr alloys, but provides no data or discussion on radiation tolerance, defect sink behaviour, or swelling reduction. The key premise linking TiC to enhanced radiation tolerance is therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: In-situ TiC precipitates form in WTaTiVCr-based alloys during spark plasma sintering at ~1600 °C with Ti and C present.
TiC precipitates provide dispersion strengthening, improving hardness and strength.
Nano-TiC precipitates can act as stable defect sinks to reduce radiation-induced swelling and defect accumulation.
The beneficial mechanical and radiation-tolerance effects can be achieved simultaneously in a single alloy.
